dependency_coverage.name: Fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: A type equipped with finite-type data, so that all of its elements form a finite collection.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Requires the index type to be finite, making its cardinality and the finite indexed family of sets relevant to the bound.

dependency_coverage.name: Fintype.card
dependency_coverage.meaning: The natural-number cardinality of a type carrying a Fintype instance, defined as the cardinality of the universal finite set.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the factor counting the indices; this natural number is later cast to a real and multiplied by q.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: The multiplication operation selected by an HMul typeclass instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applies real multiplication to the real cast of the index cardinality and q in the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: The binary less-than-or-equal relation supplied by an LE typeclass instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Expresses both the per-index upper-bound hypotheses and the final upper-bound conclusion using the usual order on the reals.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasurableSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: A measurable-space structure on a type, specifying its measurable sets.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the measurable structure required to form a measure on Ω; the proposition does not separately assume that any Bad i is measurable.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure
dependency_coverage.meaning: A measure on a measurable space, with values ordinarily taken in the extended nonnegative reals.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Introduces the arbitrary measure μ used to evaluate every Bad i and their indexed union.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.real
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a measure μ and set s, the real number obtained by applying ENNReal.toReal to the extended-nonnegative-real value μ(s). In particular, an infinite value is sent to 0 by toReal.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: All bounds concern this real conversion of measure values, rather than the original extended-nonnegative-real values; this is semantically consequential when a measured set has infinite measure.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat.cast
dependency_coverage.meaning: The canonical conversion of a natural number into a type with a NatCast instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Converts the finite cardinality of ι into a real number for multiplication by q.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The common bound q, converted measure values, order comparisons, and cardinality-times-q bound all live in the real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: The standard less-than-or-equal order instance on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes every displayed inequality an ordinary real inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: The standard multiplication instance on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Makes the right-hand side of the conclusion the ordinary real product (card ι : ℝ) * q.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instNatCast
dependency_coverage.meaning: The standard embedding of natural numbers into the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Interprets the natural cardinality of ι as its corresponding nonnegative integer-valued real.

dependency_coverage.name: Set
dependency_coverage.meaning: A set of elements of α, represented as a predicate α → Prop.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Each Bad i is an arbitrary subset of Ω, and the conclusion measures their union.

dependency_coverage.name: Set.iUnion
dependency_coverage.meaning: The indexed union of a family of sets, defined as their supremum in the set lattice; it contains exactly the points lying in at least one member of the family.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Forms the set ⋃ i, Bad i whose real-converted measure is bounded in the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: The homogeneous HMul instance induced by a multiplication operation on one type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Selects ordinary real multiplication for the cardinality factor and q.

binders: A type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A finite type ι of indices.
An arbitrary measure μ on Ω.
A family Bad : ι → Set Ω of subsets of Ω.
hypotheses: For every index i in ι, the real conversion of μ(Bad i) is at most q.
conclusions: The real conversion of the measure of the indexed union ⋃ i, Bad i is at most (cardinality of ι, viewed as a real number) times q.
mathematical_definitions: For any set s, the expression μ.real(s) means ENNReal.toReal(μ(s)), not an independently real-valued measure.
The set ⋃ i, Bad i consists of the elements of Ω that lie in Bad i for at least one i in ι.
The factor card(ι) is the finite number of elements of ι and is canonically cast from a natural number to a real before multiplication.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every measurable space Ω, every finite index type ι, every measure μ on Ω, every family of sets Bad indexed by ι, and every real q, if each set has real-converted measure at most q, then the real-converted measure of their union is at most |ι| q.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type must be finite; this proposition does not state a countable-union bound.
The same scalar q bounds every member of the family; there are no separate per-index bounds or a sum of varying bounds.
The sets Bad i are arbitrary subsets, with no explicit measurability assumptions.
The measure μ is arbitrary: there is no probability normalization, finiteness, sigma-finiteness, independence, or other probabilistic assumption.

Because Measure.real applies ENNReal.toReal, an infinite measure value is converted to 0. Thus the statement can discard infinite-measure information and should not be read unconditionally as a bound on the original extended-valued measure.

The real number q has no explicit nonnegativity hypothesis. If ι is nonempty, a negative q makes the per-index hypothesis impossible because Measure.real values are nonnegative, so the implication is vacuous in that case.
If ι is empty, the per-index hypothesis is vacuous, the indexed union is empty, and the conclusion reduces to 0 ≤ 0 because card(ι) = 0.
